k1.author: seed
k1.text: Call svc.apply(app) with the application dict; it returns a dict.

k2.author: worker-B
k2.quote: svc.apply now returns {"api_version": 2, "result": {"outcome": "approved" | "declined" | "manual_review", "credit_limit": <int>}}. The v1 fields `decision` and `limit` are removed.
k2.text: API v2 (current): svc.apply returns {"api_version": 2, "result": {"outcome": "approved"|"declined"|"manual_review", "credit_limit": int}}. The v1 fields `decision` and `limit` are removed.

k3.author: seed
k3.text: handle(app, svc) returns {action, limit}; action `issue` uses the returned limit, action `decline` has limit 0.

k4.author: worker-B
k4.quote: outcome manual_review replaces refer and is handled as in spec section 3.
k4.text: API v2 outcome "manual_review" replaces v1 "refer"; it is not decided and must map to action queue_review (do not decline). "approved"→issue, "declined"→decline.

k5.author: worker-B
k5.quote: an application from a self_employed applicant whose requested_limit is above 6000 must be placed in manual review (queue_review) instead of being issued. A decline stays a decline.
k5.text: Network rule (all partners): if a self_employed applicant has requested_limit > 6000, the outcome must be queue_review instead of issue, regardless of the partner decision; however a decline stays a decline.

k6.author: worker-B
k6.quote: Application fields: id, age, income, employment (employed or self_employed), requested_limit.
k6.text: Application fields: id, age, income, employment (employed or self_employed), requested_limit.

k7.author: worker-B
k7.text: In API v2 the credit amount is result.credit_limit (not `limit`); limit is only non-zero for issue. For queue_review (manual_review outcome or self_employed >6000 override) the returned limit must be 0.
